title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal II Problem

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000].
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]
content.problemStatement:
With the `root` of a binary tree, output *the bottom-up level order traversal of its nodes' values*. (i.e., from left to right, level by level from leaf to root).

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/02/19/tree1.jpg)

```
Input: root = [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]
Output: [[15,7],[9,20],[3]]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: root = [1]
Output: [[1]]
```

**Example 3:**

```
Input: root = []
Output: []
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[0, 2000]`.
* `-1000 <= Node.val <= 1000`

solution.approach: The approach uses a breadth-first search (BFS) to traverse the binary tree level by level, storing the node values in a list of lists, and then reversing the list to achieve the bottom-up order.

hidden.label: Last level has one leftmost node
Last level has one rightmost node
Last level has two separated leaves
All maximum values with sparse children
Irregular tree with deep mixed branches
